page: Vultr vcg-a40-1c-5g-2vram is a fractional GPU instance belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features a single dedicated Intel x86_64 CPU core running at 2.0 GHz with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 5.0 GB of system memory and 90 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, delivering 2 GB of dedicated VRAM, representing approximately 0.0417 of a full A40 GPU. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between general compute and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1302.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1713.88, both falling in the average tier. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are poor, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1303.0 and large-block memory write bandwidth limited to 10.61 GB/sec. Conversely, the fractional GPU excels at lightweight machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier LLM inference speeds of 9931.92 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 454.57 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M model, alongside strong prompt processing of 211.23 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

This instance offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for developers requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. The resource density is tailored for lightweight workloads that benefit from hardware acceleration but do not require massive CPU or memory resources. It is highly suited for small-scale LLM inference, model prototyping, and basic single-threaded tasks. It is poorly suited for database operations, multi-threaded compilation, high-throughput web serving, or memory-intensive applications due to its single-core limitation and weak memory performance.
